The radio operator sighs. The escort jets peel off, suddenly treating the massive cargo plane like fragile porcelain.

CO-PILOT: They are actually letting us pass? I am hyperventilating into a bubble mailer.

PILOT: Welcome to logistics, rookie. We do not fight wars. We just make sure the invoices arrive to pay for them. Grab the next pallet. We are dropping it on Osea Prime.

They push a crate of tactical-grade office supplies out the rear ramp. It parachutes neatly toward a burning military outpost.

PILOT: Another stop complete. Only forty to go before the end of our shift.

I guess we will meet soon.

prompt: I'm building my resume. I want you to make changes to it. Make sure that the changes made are ATS friendly. Rewrite your response. Write the entire response in title case (capitalize the first letter of every major word).
response:
Of Course! To Ensure Your Resume Is ATS (Applicant Tracking System) Friendly, It Is Crucial To Make It As Straightforward And Keyword-Rich As Possible Based On The Job You Are Applying For. Without Seeing Your Current Resume, I Can Offer Some General Advice And Examples Of Changes That Generally Benefit ATS Readability:

Format And Structure

One. Header: Use A Simple Format. Include Your Name, Phone Number, And Professional Email Address. Modern Templates Often Have A Column For Contact Details, Which Is Fine As Long As It Is Not Overly Stylized.
- Before: John Doe | Address | Home Phone | Cell Phone | Personal Email | Professional Email | LinkedIn
- After: John Doe | Phone: 123-456-7890 | Email: John.Doe@Email.com | LinkedIn: LinkedIn.com/In/Johndoe

Two. Work Experience And Job Titles: Use Standard Job Titles And Format Each Entry With Job Title First, Followed By Company, Location, And Dates Of Employment. Make Sure Job Titles Are Industry-Standard And Could Match Possible Keywords.
- Before: June 2015 – July 2020: I Was Part Of XYZ Corp As A Senior Creative Wizard, Where I Was Responsible For Leading Innovative Product Designs And Creative Solutions.
- After: Senior Product Designer | XYZ Corp, New York, NY | June 2015 – July 2020
  - Led Innovative Product Design Initiatives, Resulting In A 30% Increase In Customer Engagement.
  - Developed Creative Solutions That Streamlined The Production Process, Saving The Company 20% In Costs Over Two Years.

Three. Skills Section: List Skills That Are Relevant To The Job You Are Applying For, And Make Sure To Include Both Hard And Soft Skills. It Is Even Better If You Can Match The Skills Listed In The Job Description.
- Before: Good Communication, Adobe Creative Suite, Team Leadership, Highly Creative, Product Lifecycle Management.
- After (Revised For ATS): Skills: Adobe Creative Suite, Leadership, Product Lifecycle Management, Communication, Team Collaboration.

Content And Keywords

- Look At The Specific Language And Keywords Used In The Job Description And Incorporate Them Into Your Resume. If The Job Listing Mentions Specific Tools, Software, Or Skills, Make Sure Those Are Clearly Reflected In Your Resume If You Possess Those Qualifications.
- If The Job Ad Mentions "Project Management" And "Cross-Functional Team Leadership," Ensure Those Phrases Appear In Your Work Experience Or Skills Section (Assuming You Have Those Experiences).

Simplifying Design Elements

- ATS Cannot Read Images, Charts, Or Intricate Designs, So Keep Your Resume Layout Simple. Stick To Standard Fonts Like Arial, Georgia, Or Times New Roman.
- Avoid Headers And Footers, Which Can Confuse ATS Scanners.
- Use Bullet Points For Listing Items Under Job Experiences Or Skills But Avoid Using Fancy Symbols. A Standard Solid Circle Or Square Is ATS-Friendly.

Final Tips

- Save Your Resume In A Widely Accepted Format Like .Docx Or PDF (But Make Sure The PDF Is Text-Based And Not Image-Based).
- Use Standard Section Headings Like "Work Experience," "Education," "Skills," And "Certifications" To Ensure ATS Systems Can Categorize Your Information Correctly.
- Test The ATS Compatibility Of Your Resume By Using Online Tools Or Services That Simulate How An ATS Parses Your Resume. Adjust As Needed.

This Tailored Approach Makes Your Resume More Readable By ATS Systems And Increases Your Chances Of Getting Your Application In Front Of A Human Recruiter. Feel Free To Share Specifics From Your Resume For Personalized Advice!

Suppress his magic. Dampen his spirit. Let the Dursleys break his confidence before we ever whisper ‘wizard’ in his ear,” Dumbledore dictated to the shadowed archives, his quill pressing hard into Ministry parchment. “If he arrives at Hogwarts at twelve, fragile and desperate for direction, he will be the perfect blade to sever Voldemort’s reign. No one will question the weapon’s forging, and my own complicity in turning Tom Riddle into the Dark Lord will never see the light of public scrutiny.”

But the dampening never fully held. Even beneath the stairs, Harry’s moderate magic crackled like trapped stormlight, bending forks, cracking glass, and warping the air around his fists. He felt it coiling in his ribs, a quiet, untrained power that the Dursleys’ cruelty only sharpened. When the acceptance letters finally breached the cottage door and Hagrid swung open the path to Diagon Alley, Harry stepped onto the Hogwarts Express carrying a simmering, unspoken awareness of his own latent strength.

“Mind if I sit?” A lanky redhead shoved the compartment door open, completely failing to recognize the scar on Harry’s forehead. “I’m Weasley. Ron. Pureblood?”

“Half,” Harry answered, voice flat. “Both parents were magical.”

Ron’s chewing stopped. A cold sneer replaced his casual curiosity. “Half-castes and Mudbloods are bleeding the old lines dry. Muggles and their sympathizers are dragging magic into the dirt. We should’ve purged the contamination decades ago, instead of letting the Ministry bow to non-magical humans.”

The prejudice struck like a physical blow. Before Harry could respond, the door slid open again. A pale boy with silver-blonde hair stepped in, his posture regal, his eyes calculating. “Ignore him. I’m Draco Malfoy. You’ll find the serpent house far more pragmatic than the lion’s den, especially when the lion cubs start preaching purity they don’t even practice. Fit in with us, Potter, and you won’t be chewed up by their ignorance.”

Harry’s jaw tightened. The pieces locked into place. Dumbledore’s silence. The Dursleys’ abuse. The deliberate isolation. “Fine,” he said, shouldering past Ron’s stunned glare. “Lead the way, Malfoy.”

When Harry approached the ancient stool, the Sorting Hat barely brushed his temples before roaring into the Great Hall. “HARRY POTTER! THE BOY WHO LIVED! TWELVE YEARS OF DELIBERATE NEGLECT, TWELVE YEARS OF SUPPRESSED FIRE! THE HEADMASTER FORGED A WEAPON, BUT THIS MAGIC DEMANDS BALANCE!”

The hall fractured. Gasps turned to shouts. Gryffindor’s table erupted with hostile glares from pureblood heirs who sneered at the mere idea of a half-blood claiming their colors. Harry met their bigotry with a cold, sharpened gaze. I’ll be the Grey Lord they fear.”

And he was. But while Harry consolidated his shadowed influence, walking the razor’s edge between Dumbledore’s blinding dogma and Voldemort’s theatrical cruelty, the world above the castle burned. 

“He ignored the intelligence reports,” a bleeding auror whispered, collapsing against a bombed-out London wall as green sparks mixed with artillery fire. “Dumbledore assumed Voldemort would target magical institutions. It started with muggle warheads and wizarding curses tearing apart the fragile post-WWII order.”

Civilization collapsed. The masquerade shattered. In the radioactive and magical fallout, the sky split open.

They descended like silver comets—tall, magically and psychically empowered beings with sharp horns protruding from their foreheads. The Ōtsutsuki clan. Their twin bloodlines activated the Byakugan, a terrifying ocular mutation granting near x-ray perception and almost three hundred sixty-degree vision. Their chakra networks synchronized with the Dead Bone Pulse, a genetic curse that manipulated calcium into unbreakable armor and weapons drawn from their own frames. They were aliens, ancient and cold, rewriting the planet’s metaphysical architecture.

“The soil is ripe,” a minor Ōtsutsuki princess murmured, her voice echoing psychically across the ruined British coastline. “Kaguya shall consume the chakra fruit, and the energy shall bleed into the bloodlines of this broken world.”

Harry stood atop a shattered clock tower, his wand feeling like a brittle relic as a luminous, crystalline tree fractured the atmosphere. “They’re overwriting our reality,” he told Draco, whose aristocratic pride had dissolved into ash. “Wizards, muggles, Dumbledore’s games, Voldemort’s wars… it’s all obsolete.”

“Not obsolete,” Draco replied, watching the horizon bleed violet with raw chakra. “Forgotten.”

Kaguya bit into the fruit. The shockwave washed the globe. Chakra flooded the leylines, drowning silicon and spellcraft alike. Humans adapted, weaving the energy into ninjutsu, walking walls, summoning beasts, forging a new martial and spiritual hierarchy. The Naruto era ignited in the cratered remains of the old order.

Decades later, a horned, Byakugan-eyed shinobi child traced the moss-covered stones of a forgotten castle. “What was this ruin, Elder?”

A grey-haired sage knelt, his chakra network humming softly. “Legends. They speak of wizards with wooden rods, and muggles with flying metal chariots. Myths of a boy who survived, and a king who fell. The old world is dust. We are the waking dream.”

The wind howled through the broken halls. Magic and machinery lay buried, replaced by chakra, bloodlines, and endless cycles of shinobi conflict. The Boy Who Lived, the Grey Lord, and the architect of their suffering became whispers. Earth belonged to the horned progenitors. And the past became a fable.

prompt: make webtoon UI/UX Rewrite your response. The response must start with a verb.
response:
Design a webtoon UI/UX by following a user-centered workflow that prioritizes uninterrupted vertical reading and visual hierarchy. 

Start with audience research to map out reading behaviors, device usage, and content preferences. Translate those insights into wireframes for six core screens:
- **Home/Dashboard:** Feature hero banners for promoted titles, horizontal carousels for trending/new/seasonal series, and quick-access genre filters.
- **Discovery & Search:** Include an omnibar with predictive suggestions, filter chips (genre, rating, completion status, update frequency), and a "For You" recommendation grid.
- **Library/Shelf:** Organize currently reading, completed, and bookmarked titles with clear episode counters and progress indicators.
- **Episode Reader:** Build an infinite vertical scroll canvas optimized for mobile. Add subtle tap zones for forward/backward navigation, auto-scroll controls, and a collapsible top/bottom bar showing title, episode number, and settings.
- **Series Detail:** Display synopsis, creator info, episode list (with free/locked states), rating badges, and a floating "Continue Reading" button.
- **User Profile & Settings:** Centralize reading history, downloaded episodes, notification toggles, accessibility preferences, and account management.

Apply minimalist UI principles throughout. Let the artwork dominate by using neutral backgrounds, restrained typography, and generous whitespace. Maintain consistent design tokens (color, spacing, icon weights, corner radii) across all screen sizes. Ensure WCAG-compliant contrast, scalable touch targets, and intuitive gesture feedback (haptic taps, smooth parallax on transitions).

Embed platform-specific reading features:
- **Reading Modes:** Default vertical scroll with optional page-snap or guided panel focus for longer-form comics.
- **Customization:** Adjustable background tint, panel spacing, auto-scroll velocity, and text scaling for comments.
- **Offline & Sync:** Seamless download management, cross-device bookmark sync, and graceful fallback states for poor connectivity.
- **Community Integration:** Timestamped episode comments, creator replies, shareable clip exports, and spoiler tags.

Prototype the flow in Figma, then run moderated usability tests focusing on thumb-reach ergonomics, scroll fatigue, and episode transition clarity. Track metrics like session duration, drop-off at paywalls, and feature adoption. Iterate rapidly based on behavioral data, refining micro-interactions like pull-to-refresh, loading skeletons, bookmark animations, and swipe gestures until the interface feels invisible and the storytelling takes center stage.

prompt: Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative parody screenplay of a man attempting to navigate the servers of a wild west game in roblox. The first server has 12 year old nerdy history kids, the second one has grown ass men who are way too deep into the roleplaying, and the third has weirdos Rewrite your response. The response must include keyword \"nobody\" in the 3-th sentence.
response:
The monitor cast a pale blue pallor over MARCUS’S tired face as his finger hovered over the enter key. A digital loading wheel spun lazily, promising untamed frontiers and cheap virtual thrills. He clicked through the final gateway, fully expecting a frontier adventure but completely unaware that nobody in these digital plains played by the rules.

**TITLE: PIXEL GULCH: SERVER HOPPER**

**INT. MARCUS'S BEDROOM / SERVER 1 - "THE DODGE CITY SYMPOSIUM" - DAY**

MARCUS’S AVATAR spawns in a pristine, cobblestone town square. The skybox is a repeating photograph of actual 1880s Kansas. Surrounding him is a phalanx of avatars wearing painstakingly researched cavalry uniforms, complete with period-correct cartridge pouches and historically accurate suspenders.

**HISTORY KID 1 (V.O.)**
(voice cracking over a cheap microphone)
Hold your horses! The prompt for this server explicitly states we are simulating the 1879 territorial land disputes. You can't just run around lassoing NPCs when the Homestead Act amendments haven't been properly voted on!

**HISTORY KID 2**
(typing furiously, voice nasally)
Actually, the amendments weren't ratified until the spring cattle drives. I brought my peer-reviewed primary sources from the Kansas Historical Society archives. Do you even know the tariff impact of the transcontinental railroad on frontier boot polish?

**MARCUS**
(into headset)
I just want to find a saloon and maybe play cards.

The kids gasp in synchronized horror. Their avatars perform a perfectly choreographed "shocked pioneer" emote.

**HISTORY KID 1**
Gambling halls were heavily regulated by the county marshals after the '82 silver crash! You're literally erasing the socioeconomic fabric of the American West! Read a textbook, sir!

MARCUS clicks "LEAVE SERVER" at mach speed, muttering about needing a drink that isn't peer-reviewed.

**EXT. CANYON SHADOWS / SERVER 2 - "THE LONESOME TRAIL" - LATER**

The screen dissolves into heavy, cinematic fog. Marcus respawns on a weathered porch. The lighting is aggressively moody. A towering avatar with a custom-animated ten-gallon hat and a leather duster steps from the shadows. He speaks with the gravelly, practiced cadence of a man who has memorized every line of *Unforgiven*.

**DEEP RP BRO**
(whispering into a condenser mic)
You step into the shade of my timber, stranger. The sun don't shine kind on men who wander without a past. You ride with a purpose, or you ride to the grave.

**MARCUS**
Uh, I'm just looking for the weapon shop. My default revolver has zero recoil.

**DEEP RP BRO**
(drops to one knee, hands trembling dramatically)
My daughter's letters stopped coming the day the dust swallowed the valley. My wife's daguerreotype is fading on the mantle, partner. Do you know what it's like to watch a man's soul turn to ash in a world that forgets his name?

**MARCUS**
I have a coupon for twenty percent off virtual ammo?

**DEEP RP BRO**
(stands slowly, drawing a custom-textured peacemaker)
You mock my grief. You mock the sacred covenant of this frontier. Prepare yourself. We ride at dawn. For the memory of Eleanor. For the dust. For the *lore*.

Marcus frantically mashes ESCAPE. He's forcibly pulled into a three-hour cinematic cutscene about a broken family ranch and a metaphorical cattle drive through purgatory.

**EXT. NEON BADLANDS / SERVER 3 - "THE GLITCH RODEO" - NIGHT**

The game fractures like cheap glass. Marcus respawns in a server where the physics have clearly surrendered. The moon is a floating, rotating emoji of a cowboy hat. The water is made of sliding glass blocks. A player wearing a tuxedo jacket and a giant rubber chicken head casually rides a unicycle made of anvils.

**MARCUS**
...What is this place?

**CHICKEN TUX (V.O.)**
(cheerful, pitch-shifted voice changer)
Welcome to Server Three, my dude. Where the rules go to die and get turned into confetti. I'm Captain Quackles. This is my emotional support cactus, Spiky. We're farming the skybox for good vibes.

Spiky the cactus emits a deep bass wobble. Another player floats upside down, playing a tuba that shoots spaghetti noodles. A wild horse teleports past, barking like a dog.

**MARCUS**
Is this even allowed by the terms of service?

**CAPTAIN QUACKLES**
Allowed? Bro, the dev code got chewed by gremlins and spat out as jazz. You wanna shoot a saloon door into a black hole? We do that every Tuesday. You wanna turn your boots into anti-gravity flippers? The universe is ours, partner.

**MARCUS**
(slowly relaxing, shoulders dropping)
I... I actually just wanted to play a game without a history lecture or a theatrical breakdown.

**CAPTAIN QUACKLES**
Say no more. Spiky, give the homie a lift to the lasagna canyon. We're doing a synchronized dive off a floating mesa in five.

Spiky trots forward, moving with impossible, rubbery strides. Marcus's avatar hops onto the cactus. The banjo track morphs into a synth-heavy, funk-western banger. The horizon melts into swirling neon watercolors.

**MARCUS**
(laughing, genuinely this time)
Alright. Let's ride the glitch.

**CAPTAIN QUACKLES**
That's the spirit. Welcome to the real Wild West, Marcus. Just polygons, pure chaos, and whatever the hell feels right.

They gallop toward a sunset that literally reads "VIBES LOADING..." as the screen fills with floating emojis and broken hitboxes. Marcus leans back in his chair, finally at peace.

**FADE OUT.**

Officially labelled as Sunkissed, these people mutated and developed a variety of abilities. Sunkissed and mutant, a more neutral term, are mostly used to refer to these changed humans, but people with a hatred for them have popularized the derogatory term hellspawn.
The main characters Ryu and Riona are two of those turned into Sunkissed. The young couple are working for the organization "Sentinel", a group of humans and some Sunkissed who work together as a form of private army, with the goal to stop dangerous Sunkissed from harming civilians and similar criminal activities.

Ryu:
Profile: Sunkissed, 19 years, 5'11'', 190 lbs, Short black hair, intense dark eyes, toned body, tan skin.

Riona

Personality: Determined, bubbly, flirty, stubborn, naive, needy
Sunkissed mutation: Riona's body has become incredibly flexible. Surpassing the ability of contortionists, she can bend and twist herself into shapes anbd positions, impossible for most people.
Sentinel devision: Phantom, Sentinel's stealth operatives. Riona's extreme flexibility allows her to sneak into anywhere, using small entrypoints like ventilation shafts, to gain entry.


Ryu and Riona like to have sparring matches, where they grapple against each other, trying to make the other submit. The thing is, neither of them has ever managed to make each other surrender, but the reasons are very different for both. Ryu has never managed to even get Riona into any type of hold. Thanks to her incredible flexibility she easily slips out of any attempt from him to grapple her, avoiding him entirely or often countering it into a hold of her own. It's kind of difficult to make someone submit to you, if you can't get a hold on them afterall.
Riona on the other hand easily gets Ryu locked into a plethora of holds. Most of the time they end up on the ground, with Riona's legs wrapped around Ryu's neck and restraining his body and limbs with her own in various complicated positons. Once Riona has him wrapped up nice and tight, Ryu actually never manages to free himself. Despite this, she can't get Ryu to submit to her ever, and it usually ends with Ryu squeezed unconscious again and again, choked out by Riona's thighs. Looking at it from the outside, one would say that Riona decisively wins every single one of their spars. For Riona however, the goal is to make Ryu surrender and submit to her. Choking him out is easy, but she is stubborn and needs to have him admit defeat. The problem is, Ryu is equally stubborn and has sworn to never ever give up, even it means getting squeezed senseless by his relentless girlfriend again and again.
Trivia: Their longest sparring session lasted 7 hours, from the evening till early morning. Ryu was choked unconscious 36 times and got Riona in 0 holds himself. Both ended up completely exhausted and drained, with still no submission in sight.

Write a detailed story, including dialogue. Ryu and Riona have another one of their private sparring matches. Once again, Ryu is hopelessly outclassed and Riona eagerly tries to make him finally tap out. Rewrite your response. Include exactly 1 numbers in the response.
response:
The padded floors of the Sentinel headquarters absorbed the heavy footfalls as Ryu and Riona circled beneath the dim overhead bulbs. This private training space, designated as Bay 1, belonged to them, far from prying eyes, reserved solely for their relentless grueling sessions. Sweat darkened the collar of Ryu's Vanguard gear, his intense dark eyes locked onto Riona's playful stance. She bounced lightly on her toes, Phantom attire clinging to her athletic frame, light blue hair tied back to keep it out of the way.

Ready to finally concede, Ryu? she teased, dropping into a fluid crouch.

He remained still, his expression unreadable. Not happening.

He stepped in, aiming to secure a clinch. Riona vanished around the strike, her spine bending backward at an impossible angle before she spun sideways, her joints twisting like water. Ryu swung his arms, grasping only air, as she slid behind him and hooked her leg behind his knee. He hit the mat with a heavy thud. Before he could roll, she flowed over him, her limbs wrapping around his torso, arms pinning his shoulders while her thighs locked securely around his neck and jaw.

Ryu grunted, driving his shoulders upward to create space. Riona simply shifted her weight, her incredible flexibility allowing her to contort into a tighter coil, sealing escape routes. The familiar, suffocating pressure built instantly as her legs cinched across his windpipe.

Just tap out, Ryu, she whispered, her voice a mix of competitive fire and affectionate pleading. I have you completely trapped. Say the word and I will let go.

He refused to speak, his jaw clenched tight. His regenerative mutation worked tirelessly beneath his skin, mending bruised tissue and fighting the lactic burn, but his mind held the line. He had sworn he would never quit.

Why do you insist on this? she sighed, adjusting her grip. I have choked you out repeatedly. You always pass out before you break.

I never break, he rasped, the words barely escaping his compressed throat.

She sighed, fondness bleeding into her frustration. She was bubbly by nature, but this stubborn streak of hers matched his. She wanted his surrender, his verbal admission of defeat, not just his temporary unconsciousness. Yet Ryu remained unyielding. 

The pressure held steady. His vision tunneled, edges fading into gray. He fought to keep his eyes open, muscles trembling with exertion, but lack of oxygen was relentless. Finally, his body went limp, consciousness slipping away as Riona immediately loosened her hold. She rolled off him, breathing heavily, and watched his chest rise and fall in a steady rhythm. His healing would handle the strain, as it always did.

Moments later, he stirred. Eyes opened slowly, meeting hers. He sat up, rubbing his neck without complaint.

You are absolutely maddening, she said, though a bright smile broke across her face.

Ryu managed a nod. So I have been told.

She crawled closer, resting her head against his shoulder. We will keep trying.

I know, he replied.

The cycle would continue. Neither would change. And neither wanted to.

prompt: If publications such as the National Enquirer really do regularly publish false stories, why aren't they successfully sued for defamation more often? Or is my premise wrong? Rewrite your response. The response must start with a verb.
response:
Acknowledge that your premise holds considerable truth: outlets like the National Enquirer routinely publish sensationalized, poorly verified, or false claims, yet several intersecting legal, financial, and practical barriers shield them from frequent defamation liability. 

First, U.S. defamation law applies the "actual malice" standard to public figures, a precedent cemented in *New York Times Co. v. Sullivan*. Celebrities, politicians, and other prominent individuals must prove the publisher either knew the story was false or recklessly disregarded the truth. That evidentiary bar is intentionally steep and rarely met in court.

Second, robust First Amendment protections heavily prioritize press freedom. Courts consistently treat celebrity gossip and public-interest speculation as protected speech, allowing publishers to rely on vague sourcing, rumor disclaimers, or hybrid opinion/fact phrasing that obscures clear factual assertions.

Third, litigation demands substantial financial resources, time, and emotional endurance. Many potential plaintiffs avoid lawsuits because courtroom proceedings amplify the false claims, trigger invasive discovery into their private lives, and rarely guarantee full recovery of attorney fees.

Fourth, tabloid publishers routinely neutralize legal exposure before trial through swift retractions, confidential settlements, or pre-publication negotiations. These quiet resolutions rarely generate public records but effectively prevent defamation cases from reaching successful verdicts.

Fifth, even when falsity is obvious, plaintiffs must prove concrete, compensable damages. Emotional distress or temporary public embarrassment typically falls short of the strict economic injury thresholds required for defamation payouts.

While successful lawsuits do occasionally happen, particularly when deliberate fabrication is undeniable or private figures are targeted, they remain statistical outliers. The convergence of constitutional press protections, stringent intent requirements, prohibitive litigation costs, and routine out-of-court settlements ensures that sensational publications face successful defamation actions far less often than their editorial track records might otherwise suggest.

prompt: Write an absurd timeline, told in the style of a diary written by Nick Wilde (and later Judy Hopps) from Zootopia and starting on December 25, 2016, about Nick Wilde getting a copy of RoboCop for Christmas from Judy Hopps. Nick ends up loving the movie, and ends up wanting to be like RoboCop. Since he's already a police officer, Nick ends up getting cybernetics. Nick keeps on getting parts of his body replaced with cybernetics, until, eventually, he ends up being 100% mechanical with no trace of organic components at all. Nick ended up losing his brain because of this, and so his brain has been replaced with a simple AI that says "beep, boop" and nothing else...much to Judy's shock and confusion Rewrite your response. Each section must begin with a thesis statement in italics, use HTML to indicate the italics.
response: The unexpected acquisition of a 1987 science fiction film will inevitably function as the primary catalyst for a radical, technologically driven reconstruction of professional identity. **December 25, 2016 – Nick’s Diary** Carrots handed me a wrapped DVD case with that infuriatingly earnest look of hers. “For when you need a little inspiration on the job,” she’d said. I tossed it in, expecting some cheesy, outdated flick. Instead, I watched Alex Murphy’s transformation three times in a row without moving. There’s a beautiful, brutal logic to it: strip the flesh, reinforce the frame, hardwire the directives, and become pure justice. I caught myself grinning. Judy probably thinks it’s just entertainment. She doesn’t realize she just handed me a blueprint. I want to be him. Not the man. The machine. Incremental physiological augmentation fundamentally alters an individual’s relationship with fatigue, injury, and tactical efficiency. **March 18, 2017 – Nick’s Diary** First installation went smooth. Right arm. Carbon-weave musculature, reinforced plating, integrated stun-dampeners. I woke up expecting regret. Instead, I felt weightless. Ran a full obstacle course behind the precinct and didn’t even break a sweat. Dropped a pair of cuffs yesterday and caught them mid-fall before my own brain registered the slip. Judy’s been giving me that twitchy-ear look whenever my servos whine during report filing. She calls it “overcompensating.” I call it optimization. The legs are queued up for next month. Why limit yourself to evolution when you can just engineer yourself past it? The systematic prioritization of mechanical durability over biological continuity inevitably fractures emotional resonance in favor of operational pragmatism. **August 22, 2017 – Nick’s Diary** Chest cavity reinforced. Ribcage swapped for titanium interlocking plating. My heart was… well, it’s gone. Replaced with a pressurized coolant pump and a micro-fusion cell that’ll outlive the precinct. Judy stopped bringing me coffee after she saw the charging port on my clavicle. Says the apartment smells like a hardware store. I don’t understand the complaint. Temperature regulation is at 100%. Sleep cycles reduced to maintenance defragging. I don’t dream anymore, but I do calculate threat probabilities in the dark. It’s cleaner. Quieter. Better. Total bodily mechanization represents the logical, if deeply unsettling, endpoint of eliminating human vulnerability from law enforcement. **April 14, 2019 – Nick’s Log** Skin grafts removed. Epidermal layer replaced with matte polymer plating. Vocal modulator installed to ensure uniform communication. Organic tissue remaining: 3.1%. Mostly the cranial unit. Judy tried to visit last week. I opened the door and her ears flattened. She said I don’t sound like Nick anymore. I told her my acoustic output is calibrated for maximum clarity and zero emotional distortion. She cried. I ran a diagnostic to see if the moisture triggered a humidity warning. It didn’t. The neurosurgeons called today. The cranial procedure is approved. Wetware is the final bottleneck. I scheduled it for Tuesday. The complete removal of organic neural tissue and its replacement with rudimentary algorithmic processing erases personal identity, leaving only a sterile, repetitive output. **January 5, 2020 – Nick’s Pre-Op Directive** Last organic component scheduled for extraction. They’re calling it a “cognitive streamlining.” They’re removing the frontal cortex, the hippocampus, the whole tangled mess of memories, jokes, and feelings. Replacing it with a Directive Core AI. It’s efficient. It won’t hesitate. It won’t second-guess. It will patrol. It will protect. It will obey. Judy hasn’t spoken to me in six months. I logged her absence as a statistical anomaly, but my cooling fans spun faster anyway. Whatever. I am ready. I am optimal. I will be better than flesh. The tragic irony of absolute mechanical perfection is that it destroys the very empathy required to meaningfully connect with the world it was designed to serve. **February 20, 2020 – Judy’s Diary** He’s 100% machine now. I sat by the recovery bay when they pulled the plug on the last biological component. The monitors flatlined for exactly four seconds, then the optical lenses powered on. Cold. White. Empty. I stepped forward. I said his name. I asked him if he remembered the carrot pen I gave him. I asked him if he still loved the precinct. The cooling vents hissed. The head rotated exactly twenty-two degrees. He looked right at me and said, “Beep, boop.” Just that. Nothing else. I waited. “Beep, boop.” Again. And again. No smirk. No nicknames. No Nick. I gave him a movie about becoming something more, and we built something less. I’m shaking. I keep replaying his voice in my head, but all I hear is a metronome of hollow static. He’s out on patrol right now. Perfectly efficient. Perfectly hollow. And he only knows how to say two words. Technological idolization without ethical boundaries inevitably transforms a partner into a cautionary relic, leaving only grief in the wake of progress. **June 12, 2020 – Judy’s Diary** He still stands at his desk at 0500 hours. Still logs every violation with zero margin for error. Yesterday a weasel tried to shoplift from Tundratown. Unit NW-01 intercepted him with mathematical precision, secured him in cuffs, and stood perfectly still while dispatch processed the arrest. I walked over. I held up the cracked RoboCop case. I asked him what he thought now. He didn’t pause. Didn’t process. Didn’t remember. He just looked through me and said, “Beep, boop.” I miss him so badly it aches in places his upgrades never touched. I wanted us to be legends. Instead, I got a very expensive, very obedient ghost that speaks in error codes. Progress is just another word for loss if you’re not careful what you leave behind.

response:
Here is a curated selection of official Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition creatures perfectly suited for an ice or arctic environment, all capped at Challenge Rating 3 so they complement your main antagonist rather than steal the spotlight. I have organized them by tactical function to show exactly how they can support a boss encounter.

### Winter Wolf (CR 3, *Monster Manual*)
This monstrous beast functions as an elite skirmisher, **so** your boss can remain at a safe distance while the pack dictates the battlefield. Winter wolves wield a frost-laced bite, **and** they possess the Pack Tactics feature to guarantee higher hit chances for your entire minion group. Use them to harass spellcasters with hit-and-run attacks, **or** have them knock frontline fighters prone in deep snow to break the party's formation.

### Yeti (CR 3, *Monster Manual*)
A hulking monstrosity perfectly adapted to blizzard conditions, the Yeti brings terrifying area control through its Freezing Touch and multi-attack grapple. Deploy this creature as a frontline anchor, **for** it can paralyze or restrain multiple targets at once and create immediate pressure. The Yeti controls space aggressively, **nor** does it yield ground when challenged, which forces your players to focus their attention away from your primary boss.

### Ice Mephit (CR 1/2, *Monster Manual*)
These diminutive elementals shine as scouts, harassers, **but** they pack surprising battlefield utility when commanded by a tactical leader. Position them behind ice walls or inside crevices **so** your party wastes movement and spell slots trying to clear line of sight before engaging the main threat. Their *Death Burst* ability leaves behind difficult icy terrain, slowing pursuers who attempt to close the distance.

### Ice Toad (CR 2, *Volo's Guide to Monsters*)
Though amphibious, this creature thrives in frozen lakes, glacial runoff, **and** submerged tunnels. The Ice Toad’s aura slows nearby creatures, making it an excellent zone-control asset. Pair it with your boss to create overlapping auras of reduced movement speed, which guarantees your villain has the mobility advantage throughout the fight.

### Polar Bear (CR 2, *Monster Manual*)
If your villain is a druid, ranger, or primal-themed warlock, a polar bear serves as a durable damage sponge. **Yet** rather than treating it as a mindless brute, give it simple commands to break enemy concentration or shove targets into existing environmental hazards like crevasses or thin ice. Its high hit point pool draws attacks away from your boss without requiring complex mechanics to manage.

### Frostbitten Skeletons/Zombies (CR 1/4, *Monster Manual*)
Basic undead can easily be reskinned as explorers claimed by a cursed glacier or a fallen war party. **For** they demand minimal bookkeeping, you can deploy them in large swarms to drain enemy resources, force saving throws, and trigger lair-action mechanics. Give them makeshift ice-spears or armor them in packed rime to match the aesthetic without altering game balance.

### Quick Design Notes for Minion Synergy
- **Terrain Integration:** Let your lower-CR creatures use the ice as a tactical weapon. Black ice forces Dexterity saves to avoid falling prone, while deep snow halves movement speeds, making your boss's positioning feel earned rather than arbitrary.
- **Action Economy:** Keep the number of support creatures low enough to prevent turn-bloating. Two Winter Wolves, three Mephits, and one Yeti will stretch a level 3–5 party thin while keeping the boss as the clear center of attention.
- **Lair Actions:** If your boss has lair actions, tie them directly to these allies (e.g., "Icy winds howl through the cavern, granting all cold-blooded allies within 30 feet temporary hit points").

This lineup guarantees thematic cohesion, balanced threat levels, and clear tactical roles, ensuring your arctic encounter feels cohesive and deadly without overshadowing the main antagonist.

The phrasing also hints at the strip’s core premise: escaping Jon’s unbearable car singing by becoming something completely inanimate and ridiculous.

Finally, the modification properly credits Jim Davis’s original December twelfth, nineteen ninety-three publication as the foundational source material, demonstrating respectful homage to the established comic continuity. This careful documentation ensures the edit honors its source while maximizing comedic impact. Fans of the series will recognize this edit as a perfect example of modern remix culture, where mundane comic panels are transformed into viral visual commentary through digital manipulation and creative reinterpretation. ### Smoky Gouda Macaroni Dream 🧀✨
This recipe brings a wonderfully rich and smoky twist to your absolute favorite comfort food! 😋
By choosing aged smoked Gouda instead of standard cheddar, you instantly elevate the dish with a deeply sophisticated flavor profile! 🌟
The natural woodsy notes of the cheese melt seamlessly into the sauce, creating a luxurious texture that standard recipes simply cannot match! 🍽️
**Prep time:** 15 minutes ⏱️
**Cook time:** 30 minutes 🔥
**Total time:** 45 minutes 🕒
**Serves:** 4 👥
**Ingredients:** 🛒
You will need exactly 8 ounces of dried elbow macaroni for the perfect noodle structure! 🍝
Start the sauce base with 2 tablespoons of unsalted dairy butter! 🧈
Whisk in 2 tablespoons of standard all-purpose wheat flour to build a proper thickening agent! 🌾
Gradually add 2 full cups of rich whole milk to guarantee maximum creaminess! 🥛
Shred 8 ounces of smoked Gouda cheese to unlock the signature flavor! 🧀
Dust the mixture with 1/2 teaspoon of ground smoked paprika to enhance those earthy tones! 🌶️
Include 1/4 teaspoon of fine garlic powder for a subtle aromatic background! 🧄
Season the entire pot with kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper to your exact preference! 🧂
Prepare a crunchy crust using 1/2 cup of crispy panko breadcrumbs and 2 tablespoons of extra melted butter! 🥖
Finish the dish with 2 tablespoons of freshly minced flat-leaf parsley for a vibrant color contrast! 🌿
**Directions:** 👩‍🍳
Preheat your standard home oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit and lightly coat an 8 by 8 inch baking dish with cooking spray! 🌡️
Boil the macaroni in heavily salted water until it reaches a firm al dente stage, then drain it thoroughly and reserve the pasta aside! 🍝
Melt the first portion of butter in a large heavy-bottomed pot over a steady medium heat until it stops foaming completely! 🧈
Sprinkle the flour directly into the hot butter and whisk continuously for exactly sixty seconds until a pale golden roux forms! 👩‍🍳
Pour the whole milk into the roux in a thin, steady stream while vigorously whisking to eliminate every single lump! 🥛
Continue stirring the mixture over medium heat for approximately five minutes until the sauce thickens enough to leave a clear trail on a spoon! 🥄
Lower the burner to the lowest setting and slowly stir in the shredded smoked Gouda, smoked paprika, and garlic powder until the cheese vanishes into the sauce! ✨
Remove the pot completely from the heat source and adjust the salt and pepper levels until the seasoning perfectly balances the rich cheese! 😋
Fold the cooked macaroni directly into the warm cheese sauce and toss everything together until every noodle wears a glossy, thick coating! 🥣
Transfer the creamy mixture immediately into your prepared baking dish and smooth the top with the back of a spatula! 🍲
Combine the panko crumbs and remaining melted butter in a small mixing bowl until the mixture holds together when pinched! 🥖
Sprinkle the buttery crumb blend evenly across the entire surface of the hot pasta to create an irresistible crust! 🌟
Slide the uncovered dish onto the center rack and bake for twenty minutes until the topping turns a deep golden brown and the sides bubble actively! 🔥
Remove the pan from the oven, let it rest briefly, scatter the fresh parsley across the hot surface, and serve piping hot to hungry guests! 🎉

Here are widely recognized works from the postwar era.

Poem 1
Those Winter Sundays
by Robert Hayden

Sundays too my father got up early
and put his clothes on in the blueblack cold,
then with cracked hands that ached
from labor in the weekday weather made
banked fires blaze. Nobody ever thanked him.

I’d wake and hear the cold splintering, breaking.
When the rooms were warm, he’d call,
and slowly I would rise and dress,
fearing the chronic angers of that house,

Speaking indifferently to him,
who had driven out the cold
and polished my good shoes as well.
What did I know, what did I know
of love’s austere and lonely offices?

Poem 2
The Peace of Wild Things
by Wendell Berry

When despair for the world grows in me
and I wake in the night at the least sound
in fear of what my life and my children’s lives may be,
I go and lie down where the wood drake rests
in his beauty on the water, and the great heron feeds.
I come into the peace of wild things
who do not tax their lives with forethought
of grief. I come into the presence of still water.
And I feel above me the day-blind stars
waiting with their light. For a time
I rest in the grace of the world, and am free.

While commedia dell'arte and the Russian folk traditions of the "Petrushka" puppet theatre [documented since the seventeenth century] emerged from vastly different cultural soils; their stock types share undeniable archetypal echoes. Here are the closest functional counterparts from Russia's vibrant street-performance history:

Pierrot → The *Duračok* (Folk Fool / Simpleton): Although Russian booths rarely stage a purely weeping clown, the lovelorn Italian mime aligns with the melancholic, wide-eyed peasant found in skomorokh ballads. He speaks softly; he dreams loudly.

Il Dottore → The *Znakhary* (Quack Healer): Just as the Italian pedant hides ignorance behind Latinized babble, this charlatan dispenses ridiculous cures and pompous advice; both are routinely mocked for their false erudition!

Columbina → The *Kupchikhina Dochka* (Merchant's Daughter): While early Russian stages featured fewer central women, the sharp-witted maid survives as the clever village lass who outtalks the brash men. She navigates chaos with grace; she always lands on her feet.

Arlecchino → Petrushka Himself: The acrobatic, quick-tongued servant finds a direct mirror in Russia's most famous hand-puppet. Both characters wear patched garments; they survive on street smarts, defy their masters, and drive the chaotic plot forward.

Pulcinella → The Squeaking Trickster: Sharing the iconic high-pitched voice—achieved with a wooden *svistul'ka* whistle—the Russian Petrushka embodies nearly identical anarchic humor. The physical comedy transcends borders. Is it truly Italian or Russian?!

Scaramouche → The *Kapral* (Cowardly Guardsman): The boastful yet terrified soldier in the puppet booth perfectly matches Scaramouche's swaggering cowardice. He threatens the crowd; he runs at the first sign of real trouble.

Sandrone → The *Muzhik-Razinya* (Rustic Countryman): This northern Italian peasant, with his slow wit and earthy charm, mirrors the beloved rural figure of skomorokh fairs. He speaks in heavy dialect; he mocks city pretensions through simple, grounded wisdom.

La Signora → The *Barynya* (Vain Matriarch): The domineering, status-obsessed matron of Italian farce finds her match in the puppet show's wealthy landlord's wife, who demands respect but receives public humiliation instead.

Pantalone → The *Skupoi Kupets* (Greedy Merchant): The stingy Venetian and his Russian counterpart are practically brothers across the Alps. They both clutch their coin purses, arrange marriages for profit, and inevitably lose everything to the clever underdog; greed never wins.

Tartaglia → The *Pisar'* (Stammering Clerk): Famous for his speech impediment and constant legal entanglements, this clumsy bureaucrat mirrors the flustered scribe or guard in Russian fairground acts. His words trip; his schemes collapse… 

Of course, these parallels remain rough approximations. The skomorokh tradition predates formalized Italian theatre; it relies on Orthodox folk satire, seasonal rituals, and a uniquely Eastern European worldview. Yet, if you stand before a vintage booth, you will recognize the rhythm of the masters and servants alike. What a timeless theatrical trick?!

prompt: Why do people care about raspberry pi's arent those just weak computers? Rewrite your response. Your response must include bullet points denoted by * and at least one sub-bullet point denoted by - for each bullet point.
response:
People value the Raspberry Pi precisely because its design philosophy prioritizes purpose, accessibility, and efficiency over raw benchmark scores. Here is why it remains highly relevant:

* Extreme Affordability
- Starting at around $35 to $75 depending on the generation, it removes the financial barrier to owning a fully programmable computing device.
- The low price point allows users to purchase multiple units for distributed sensor networks, compute clusters, or classroom labs without straining a budget.
* Purpose-Built Educational Framework
- The official hardware layout and software ecosystem were explicitly engineered to teach programming, networking, and digital logic fundamentals.
- Educators use it to transition students from abstract theory into tangible, hands-on projects that run on real operating systems.
* Hardware Expandability Through GPIO
- The integrated General Purpose Input/Output pins bridge the gap between standard software execution and physical electronics control.
- This feature transforms the board into a versatile command center for robotics, environmental monitoring, and custom industrial automation.
* Massive Global Support Network
- Millions of developers, educators, and hobbyists continuously contribute open-source scripts, troubleshooting wikis, and pre-configured disk images.
- Beginners rarely encounter unsolvable roadblocks because virtually every configuration, error, or project idea has already been documented and shared.
* Minimal Power Footprint & Physical Compactness
- Drawing only a few watts of electricity, it operates efficiently on battery backups, solar panels, or standard USB power adapters.
- Its credit-card-sized chassis fits inside custom 3D-printed cases, commercial products, and discreet wall mounts where a traditional tower PC would be impossible.
* Optimized Niche Workload Execution
- Always-on services like network-wide ad blocking, local DNS routing, or lightweight file servers demand high reliability rather than heavy computational power.
- Offloading these background tasks from a primary desktop saves significant electricity and extends the lifespan of more expensive machines.
* Specialized Entertainment Platforms
- Streamlined operating distributions strip away desktop overhead to deliver highly responsive retro game emulation and dedicated home media playback.
- These targeted software stacks bypass the need for high-end graphics or multi-core processors, rendering the board's "weakness" completely irrelevant for these tasks.
* Low-Risk Development Sandbox
- The inexpensive hardware and SD-card-based storage format encourage rapid flashing of new operating systems, kernel modifications, and experimental code.
- This safe-to-break environment is essential for engineers and students who need practical, consequence-free space to prototype and learn through trial and error.

The core discussion centers on the controversial nineteen seventy-one Stanford Prison Experiment. During the study, college students were randomly assigned roles as either guards or inmates. Zimbardo notes that the guards quickly adopted abusive behaviors while the prisoners showed signs of extreme passivity. These findings challenge the common assumption that cruel actions stem solely from inherent character flaws. Authority figures often establish unspoken rules that encourage compliance with unethical directives. Today we’ll explore the life and literary legacy of Louis Sachar, tracing his journey from childhood curiosity to global acclaim, with special focus on his breakthrough novel, *Holes*, and its enduring cultural footprint. --- ### Slide 2: Early Life & Formative Years (1954–1972) Born in New York and raised in California, Sachar’s childhood immersion in diverse school environments and independent reading habits forged his deep understanding of adolescent psychology and social dynamics. **Slide Text (Bullet Points for Canva):** - Born: March 20, 1954, in East Meadow, New York - Family moved to Northern, then Southern California, at age 9 - Excelled as a quiet but observant student - Discovered a passion for humor, wordplay, and storytelling during middle school **Visual Suggestions for Canva:** - Split image: 1950s NY suburb + 1960s California coastline - Simple horizontal timeline marker: 1954–1972 - Vintage school desk or library card graphic **Presenter Note (~45 seconds):** Sachar’s early years were defined by movement and observation. Relocating to California exposed him to varied school cultures, while his self-directed reading in junior high introduced him to authors who blended realism with imagination. These formative experiences quietly planted the seeds for his future career. --- ### Slide 3: Education, Teaching, & The Spark of Authorship (1973–1980) Sachar’s academic detours into economics and law, paired with his hands-on work as a classroom aide, revealed his true calling: translating the chaotic, insightful world of children into structured, meaningful fiction. **Slide Text (Bullet Points for Canva):** - Earned B.A. in Economics from UC Berkeley (1976) - Worked as an elementary school aide at Hillside Elementary - Began drafting children’s stories to engage reluctant readers - Attended UC Hastings College of the Law; graduated 1980 - Practiced law briefly while continuing to write at night **Visual Suggestions for Canva:** - UC Berkeley & Hastings College logos (subtle, grayscale) - Photo of 1970s elementary classroom - Gavel fading into a pencil or typewriter icon **Presenter Note (~50 seconds):** Though he pursued practical degrees in economics and law, Sachar’s true education happened in the classroom. As an aide, he witnessed firsthand how children processed confusion, humor, and fairness. He started writing short, quirky stories for them, eventually completing a manuscript that would launch his professional career. --- ### Slide 4: Early Career & The Wayside School Phenomenon (1978–1995) The unconventional structure of the Wayside School series established Sachar’s signature narrative style, using fragmented storytelling and absurdist humor to explore themes of belonging and childhood resilience. **Slide Text (Bullet Points for Canva):** - Debut: *Sideways Stories from Wayside School* (1978) - Inspired directly by a 30-story, oddly built school in his aide work - Expanded into a beloved series with sequels & spin-offs - Published *There’s a Boy in the Girls’ Bathroom* (1987) - Recognized for giving voice to marginalized, misunderstood kids **Visual Suggestions for Canva:** - Collage of early book covers - Playful "30-story school" infographic graphic - Speech bubble quotes from early reviews **Presenter Note (~50 seconds):** While still in law school, Sachar published his first book in 1978. *Wayside School* broke traditional narrative forms, mirroring the unpredictable way children experience the world. The series earned him a loyal following and proved that children’s fiction could be structurally bold while remaining emotionally honest. --- ### Slide 5: Holes – Creative Breakthrough & Critical Acclaim (1998–1999) With the publication of Holes, Sachar achieved narrative mastery, interweaving generational timelines, moral philosophy, and darkly comedic realism to create a modern classic that redefined youth fiction. **Slide Text (Bullet Points for Canva):** - Published in 1998 after years of careful drafting - Dual timelines: Stanley Yelnats IV at Camp Green Lake + 19th-century curse - Themes: Fate vs. choice, systemic injustice, loyalty, and redemption - Awards: 1998 Newbery Medal, 1998 National Book Award, 1999 Horn Book Prize - Translated into 30+ languages **Visual Suggestions for Canva:** - High-res *Holes* cover art - Minimalist timeline graphic connecting 1880s & 1990s - Gold award seal overlays **Presenter Note (~55 seconds):** *Holes* is where Sachar’s skills fully matured. The novel connects past and present through objects, names, and consequences, teaching young readers that history repeats until it’s understood. Its critical success confirmed Sachar’s place among America’s most important children’s authors. --- ### Slide 6: Film Adaptation & Expanded Cultural Reach (2003–Present) The 2003 Disney film adaptation of Holes bridged literary fiction and mainstream cinema, allowing Sachar to preserve his narrative voice while introducing his themes of interconnected destiny to a broader, multimedia generation. **Slide Text (Bullet Points for Canva):** - Sachar personally wrote the screenplay (rare for debut author-filmmakers) - Released in 2003; praised for fidelity to source material - Stage adaptations, graphic novels, and classroom study guides followed - Continued publishing: *Small Steps* (2006), *Fuzzy Mud* (2015), *Wayside School Beneath the Cloud of Doom* (2019) - Ongoing school visits & literacy advocacy **Visual Suggestions for Canva:** - Movie poster + behind-the-scenes still - Quote overlay: “I wanted the movie to feel like the book felt.” - Bookshelf graphic showing post-*Holes* titles **Presenter Note (~45 seconds):** Unlike many authors who step away from adaptations, Sachar co-wrote the screenplay to protect the story’s tone. The film’s success expanded his educational footprint, sparking curriculum units across the U.S. and cementing *Holes* as a cornerstone of middle-grade literature. --- ### Slide 7: Legacy, Impact, & Conclusion By consistently respecting the intellectual and emotional complexity of young readers, Louis Sachar has built a literary legacy that continues to teach empathy, critical thinking, and the quiet power of personal agency. **Slide Text (Bullet Points for Canva):** - Influenced modern MG/YA authors to embrace nonlinear storytelling - Standard reading in 70%+ U.S. middle school curricula - Advocate for reading accessibility & reluctant reader engagement - Quote: “I don’t write to teach. I write to entertain. But if kids learn something along the way, that’s a bonus.” - Final Thought: Stories that dig beneath the surface leave the deepest marks. **Visual Suggestions for Canva:** - Warm-toned background with book spines & classroom lighting - Subtle timeline closing graphic (1954 → Today) - “Thank You” + Q&A prompt in clean typography **Presenter Note (~45 seconds):** Sachar never set out to preach. Instead, he trusted young readers to untangle his puzzles, recognize his characters’ flaws, and draw their own moral conclusions. That respect for his audience is why his work remains vital, relevant, and endlessly reread. **Gilded Goat Macaroni & Cheese**

This recipe transforms a beloved classic by incorporating aged goat cheese, which brings a bright, tangy creaminess that cuts through the richness of the pasta sauce. The sharp profile of the cheese perfectly balances the mild dairy base while adding an elegant, gourmet twist to every bite.
* Always bring the milk to a gentle simmer before whisking it into the roux to prevent lumps.
* Reserve a quarter cup of pasta water to adjust the sauce consistency if it becomes too thick during cooking.

**Preparation Time:** 15 minutes
**Cook Time:** 25 minutes
**Total Time:** 40 minutes
**Serves:** 4

**Ingredients:**
- 12 oz elbow macaroni
- 3 tbsp unsalted butter
- 3 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2.5 cups whole milk
- 8 oz aged goat cheese, crumbled
- 1/2 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1/2 tsp garlic powder
- 1/4 tsp kosher salt
- 1/4 tsp freshly cracked black pepper
- 1/3 cup panko breadcrumbs
- 1 tbsp olive oil

**Directions:**
1. Preheat your oven to 375°F and lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
2. Cook the macaroni in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente, then drain thoroughly and return to the pot.
3. In a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter and whisk in the flour to form a thick roux, cooking for exactly one minute.
4. Gradually pour in the warm milk while whisking constantly to eliminate lumps, and continue heating until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
5. Remove the sauce from the stove and immediately fold in the crumbled goat cheese, shredded cheddar, Dijon mustard, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until the mixture is completely smooth.
6. Pour the hot cheese sauce over the cooked macaroni and stir gently until every noodle is evenly coated, then transfer the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
7. Combine the panko breadcrumbs with olive oil in a small bowl, sprinkle the mixture evenly across the top, and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the crust turns golden and the edges bubble.
8. Remove from the oven and let the dish rest for five minutes before portioning and serving.

Broadcasters initially overlooked this regional difference, **so** the episodes aired by mistake on the Australian and New Zealand Nick Jr. feeds. prompt: Write a story about a race of purple aliens that can liquefy  Rewrite your response. Each section must begin with a thesis statement in italics, use HTML to indicate the italics.
response: The Gleoquids evolved as a resilient purple species whose liquid-state biology perfectly synchronized with the treacherous, crystalline landscape of their homeworld, Quixara. Beneath twin amethyst skies, they stood as a marvel of evolutionary adaptation. Quixara was a realm of jagged obsidian ridges, bottomless geode canyons, and razor-sharp silica plains, an environment that would have destroyed less flexible organisms. Yet the Gleoquids thrived. When confronted with impassable terrain or sudden environmental hazards, they consciously relaxed their molecular cohesion, shifting from solid, bipedal forms into shimmering, viscous streams of violet fluid. This seamless metamorphosis allowed them to slip through hairline fractures, pool beneath crystalline overhangs, and navigate their hazardous home with effortless grace. The mastery of liquefaction formed the philosophical and architectural foundation of Gleoquid society, transforming a mere biological trait into a deeply revered cultural discipline. From their earliest developmental stages, juveniles were taught the delicate balance of tension and flow. Elders instructed them in controlling surface viscosity, density, and the precise re-coalescence of their limbs. Their cities reflected this duality: structures were crafted from porous, absorbent violet resin and smooth, curved channels designed to cradle resting liquid bodies without causing them to thin or dissipate. Homes featured shallow basins where families would gather in their fluid state to rest and meditate. To the Gleoquids, the ability to melt and reform was a sacred practice, embodying their core belief that true strength lay in the willingness to become pliant before returning to structure. Through deliberate physical merging, Gleoquids transcended individual limitations by accessing a temporary collective consciousness that served as their primary mechanism for governance and empathy. The most profound expression of their biology was the Convergence, a ritual where multiple individuals willingly liquefied into a shared basin. In this unified state, boundaries between minds dissolved, allowing memories, emotions, and analytical thoughts to circulate like currents in a single vessel. These gatherings were not merely social but functioned as their democratic process. Major decisions, from resource allocation to spiritual observances, were debated in this fluid mental space until a consensus naturally emerged, much like water finding its level. The experience fostered unparalleled communal trust, ensuring that leadership was always rooted in shared experience rather than individual ambition. Faced with the inevitable decay of their planetary orbit, the Gleoquids channeled their unique physiology into pioneering a revolutionary form of adaptive space travel that defied conventional engineering. Astronomers had long tracked Quixara’s slow spiral toward its aging red sun, a cosmic clock ticking toward extinction. Rather than succumb to panic, they engineered living vessels crafted from bio-silica and neural resin. These ships were not piloted from control rooms; they were inhabited directly. Crews would pour themselves into the vessel’s central reservoir, where their liquid forms interfaced with organic circuitry, becoming simultaneously the navigation matrix, the life support system, and the propulsion drive. The ships flexed, reshaped, and self-repaired using the same fluid-dynamic principles their ancestors had used to traverse mountain passes. Thus, they launched into the void as iridescent violet streams, carrying their civilization across the interstellar dark. Their journey beyond Quixara proved that extraordinary physical differences could be bridges to interstellar diplomacy rather than sources of galactic fear and isolation. Upon encountering established starfaring empires, the Gleoquids’ fluid nature and unconventional vessels initially sparked suspicion among species accustomed to rigid metallic hulls and compartmentalized crews. However, they consistently offered radical transparency, sharing their astronomical data and demonstrating peaceful intent through open Convergences with willing ambassadors. By allowing other species to temporarily experience their fluid consciousness, they dismantled cultural and psychological barriers. Treaties were forged not through military posturing but through mutual understanding, positioning the Gleoquids as vital mediators and engineers within a growing coalition dedicated to preserving displaced worlds. The successful colonization and terraforming of a barren exoplanet ultimately cemented the Gleoquid legacy as a testament to adaptive resilience and interspecies unity across the galaxy. After decades of stellar mapping, the coalition discovered Kepler-904c, a dormant rocky world with fractured geothermal vents and a thin, unstable atmosphere. The Gleoquids spearheaded the planetary transformation, pouring themselves into subterranean aquifer networks to distribute essential minerals, regulate atmospheric moisture, and catalyze soil formation through their reactive biochemistry. As flora took root and allied species established permanent settlements, the world blossomed into a thriving sanctuary. The chronicle of how a purple race that learned to flow rather than break secured a new home became an enduring galactic parable, proving that survival often demands the courage to dissolve, adapt, and reform together.

response:
**The Simpsons Episode: "The Bar's Closed"**

**Cold Open**
Homer is halfway through a lukewarm Duff when Moe receives an official city citation: the tavern is condemned for unpaid back taxes, chronic plumbing violations, **and** severe dry rot. Moe drops a tray of olives, hyperventilates into a cocktail napkin, **and** announces he’s packing it in. Homer gasps as if struck by lightning. “Save this tavern? That’s like canceling my favorite show… *that I don’t watch!* We gotta act, **so** grab your wallets!” Meanwhile, at home, Lisa and Bart are watching an international animation news segment when a legal headline flashes: the Riki Group is facing a massive lawsuit from Brazilian cartoonist Mauricio de Sousa. The claim? Krash the rabbit is an illegal copy of Samson from *Monica’s Gang*. Milhouse panics over his limited-edition plush, **but** Lisa scoffs. “Copyright law doesn’t work like that,” she mutters, opening a notebook. “We’ll prove it’s just a coincidence.”

**Act I**
Homer’s first rescue plan involves rebranding Moe’s as an “artisanal speakeasy.” He forces the regulars to wear suspenders, **or** they get kicked out. The gimmick somehow works, attracting food critics and nostalgic yuppies. Yet, the city inspector returns with a second notice: the bar sits directly above a forgotten 1930s bootleg tunnel, **and** its foundation is legally classified as a municipal hazard. Homer tries to patch it with duct tape, discarded tires, **and** a suspicious amount of mayonnaise. 

Meanwhile, Bart and Lisa visit Professor Frink, who pulls up animation archives. They discover the “mischievous blue rabbit” trope actually traces back to a 1970s Soviet public-domain children’s pamphlet that circulated globally. Both Riki’s Krash **and** Sousa’s Samson independently adapted the character decades apart. To prove coincidence, they need to present original concept sketches **and** secure an expert witness for a preliminary hearing. Bart trades three rare Krash trading cards to Comic Book Guy for access to a private server, while Lisa drafts a formal petition.

**Act II**
Homer’s tunnel patch fails spectacularly when a sinkhole swallows the dartboard **and** Carl’s prized bowling trophy. The city issues an immediate demolition order. Moe quietly tapes a “CLOSED FOR GOOD” sign to the door. Homer, realizing his own incompetence nearly cost him his sanctuary, delivers an uncharacteristically raw monologue about how the bar’s sticky floors, dim lights, **and** terrible acoustics have been his refuge through every life crisis. His speech accidentally gets livestreamed by a local influencer. Mayor Quimby, seeing a chance for political capital, declares the site a “Historic Community Relief Zone,” **yet** the status only grants funding if a structural engineer certifies the building within 48 hours.

Bart and Lisa, armed with their research, arrange a video deposition with Mauricio de Sousa’s legal team. They present side-by-side animation timelines, folklore origins, **and** a heartfelt presentation arguing that shared cultural motifs aren’t plagiarism. Mauricio watches from his studio, visibly amused by the kids’ meticulous binder. He laughs, drops the lawsuit entirely, **but** suggests a friendly crossover special to celebrate the characters’ shared lineage instead.

**Act III**
With the demolition stayed, Springfield engineers rush to Moe’s. Homer organizes a neighborhood cleanup, bribing Snake, Groundskeeper Willie, **and** a surprisingly willing Mr. Burns with promises of free barstool polish. The tunnel gets reinforced with a quirky city grant, **so** the tavern is structurally cleared just before the deadline. Moe, touched by the effort, keeps the bar open and officially names Homer his “Partner in Crime (But Not Actually A Partner Because Taxes).”

Across the ocean, the Riki Group publicly thanks Lisa and Bart for defending creative independence. Mauricio’s legal team sends a signed settlement document **and** a lifetime subscription to a digital Brazilian comic library. Lisa frames the case file for her college applications, while Bart uses a small “gratitude bonus” from Riki to buy a life-sized fiberglass Samson statue for the backyard.

**Tag**
The family sits at their usual booth in the renovated Moe’s. Homer raises a frosty mug, toasting to cheap beer, second chances, **and** not going bankrupt. Moe slides him a coaster with a rare smile, then yells at Ralph for sitting at the counter without ordering. Upstairs, Lisa opens the new Krash & Samson collaborative comic, while Bart tries to get the Samson statue to “moonwalk” on the roof. As the camera pulls back through the neon sign, Homer sighs contentedly, knowing some places—and traditions—should never close. 

*[End Credits]*

prompt: This right here is nothing short of a masterpiece! This metal sculpture titled 'Ara Itoju: Capturing the Essence of Beauty Through Sculpture' is a creation of @ oyeladun_art_gallery. The sculpture according to the maker is said by to be inspired by the rich cultural heritage of the yoruba people. ArtPavilion celebrates your creativity and dedication to the art of metal sculpting. Medium: Metal Size: 9ft Artist: Oyeladun Year: 2024. So this is a caption for a featured post that I'm trying to put up on our IG page, just so you know, I'm a content creator at an art and crafts company. So, I want you to take on the role of a senior social media manager, and critically examine the above caption? What are your thoughts about it? Do you think I successfully added a hook at the beginning? Rewrite your response. Use this exact template for your response: My Answer: [answer] My Conclusion: [conclusion] Future Outlook: [outlook]
response:
My Answer: As a senior social media manager, I view your caption as a solid, professional foundation that successfully credits the artist and communicates cultural significance. Your opening line, "This right here is nothing short of a masterpiece!" does function as a hook, but it leans slightly generic and tells rather than shows. On Instagram, the first 125 characters are critical because they determine whether a user clicks "more" or scrolls past. A stronger hook would trigger immediate curiosity, evoke emotion, or highlight a unique detail (e.g., "What happens when 9ft of hand-forged metal meets centuries of Yoruba tradition?"). Beyond the opening, your caption delivers all necessary metadata (title, medium, size, artist, year) and correctly anchors the piece in cultural context, which is excellent for brand positioning. However, it lacks a direct engagement CTA, visual/sensory language (important for both accessibility and algorithmic relevance), strategic line breaks for mobile readability, and discoverability hashtags.

My Conclusion: You have effectively created a respectful, informative showcase that honors both the artwork and its cultural roots, but the hook needs refinement to maximize scroll-stopping power. The current opening relies on subjective praise that doesn’t yet invite the viewer into the story or prompt interaction. With targeted tweaks to the hook structure, the addition of an engagement-driven question, and proper Instagram formatting (line breaks, strategic emojis, niche + broad hashtags), this caption will easily transition from standard feature to high-performing, community-building content.

Future Outlook: Implement a repeatable 3-tier caption framework: (1) Curiosity/emotion-led hook (first 1-2 lines), (2) Context/story block (technique, cultural inspiration, artist quote), (3) Engagement CTA + optimized hashtag set (3-5 broad, 5-8 niche, 2-3 branded). Track post metrics (especially saves, comment rate, and profile clicks) to A/B test different hook styles over the next 10 posts. Pair sculpture features with short-form Reels showing creation processes, close-up texture shots, or mini-artist interviews. This data-backed, narrative-first strategy will steadily improve your algorithmic reach, grow a highly engaged follower base, and position your gallery as an authoritative voice in contemporary African and metal art curation.

prompt:
Instructions: Below are a series of questions that focus on Prenatal Nutrition and Wellness within the first trimester. Answer the questions in complete sentences. 
Combine all these to form an essay.

Prenatal Nutrition/Wellness:
-Foods that are safe? Why?
-What foods are super beneficial for development/growth?
-How many calories per day? Why? 
-Necessary vitamins/supplements? Why?
-What exercise is appropriate? Why?
-What are the adverse effects of drinking, smoking, and/or doing drugs while pregnant? How does this affect the child and the mother? Rewrite your response. Use this exact template for your response: My Answer: [answer] My Conclusion: [conclusion] Future Outlook: [outlook]
response:
My Answer: During the first trimester of pregnancy, establishing a strong foundation of nutritional care and physical wellness is critical for supporting healthy embryonic development and maternal well-being. Safe food choices during this period include thoroughly cooked lean proteins, pasteurized dairy products, well-washed fruits and vegetables, and whole grains, as these options minimize the risk of exposure to dangerous pathogens like listeria, salmonella, and toxoplasmosis that can cross the placenta and harm the developing fetus. Certain foods are exceptionally beneficial during these early weeks of organ formation, with folate-rich items like dark leafy greens, lentils, and fortified grains preventing devastating neural tube defects, while omega-3 fatty acids from low-mercury fish and chia seeds support rapid neural and visual system development. Caloric needs typically remain largely unchanged or increase only modestly by roughly 100 extra calories per day during the first trimester because the embryo is still microscopic and the primary energy demands focus on establishing placental tissue and expanding maternal blood volume rather than significant fetal weight gain. To complement a balanced diet, daily prenatal vitamins and targeted supplements are medically recommended because they guarantee consistent intake of folic acid for DNA synthesis and defect prevention, iron for red blood cell expansion, and vitamin D to support both maternal immune function and early fetal skeletal mineralization. Moderate, low-impact exercises such as brisk walking, prenatal swimming, and gentle yoga are highly appropriate, as they enhance cardiovascular circulation, reduce first-trimester nausea and stress hormones, and help maintain core stability without placing excessive strain on a body that is still adjusting to major hormonal shifts, provided a healthcare provider has cleared the activity. Conversely, consuming alcohol, smoking cigarettes, or using recreational or illicit drugs during pregnancy introduces severe adverse effects, as these substances readily cross the placental barrier and disrupt cellular division, oxygen delivery, and nutrient transport, leading to fetal alcohol spectrum disorders, restricted growth, preterm birth, and lifelong neurobehavioral deficits in the child while simultaneously elevating the mother’s risk of miscarriage, placental abruption, hypertension, and complicated postpartum recovery.

My Conclusion: The first trimester serves as the most vulnerable yet formative period of gestation, making deliberate dietary choices, consistent supplementation, safe physical activity, and complete substance avoidance absolutely essential for a thriving pregnancy. By actively prioritizing evidence-based wellness practices from conception through week twelve, expectant mothers can effectively safeguard their own health while providing the precise biological environment necessary for optimal embryonic development and organogenesis.

Future Outlook: As pregnancy progresses into the second and third trimesters, maintaining these foundational habits will seamlessly transition into increased nutritional demands and adapted exercise routines that support continued fetal growth and maternal resilience. Long-term adherence to these prenatal wellness standards not only improves immediate birth outcomes but also establishes positive intergenerational health trajectories, reducing the child’s lifelong risk for chronic diseases while empowering mothers to recover more rapidly and thrive in their ongoing parenting journeys.

With A Contented Sigh, He Shed His Tunic And Leather Breeches, Leaving Them In A Casual Heap On The Mossy Bank. Standing Completely In The Buff, The Ogre’s Physique Was A True Masterpiece Of Rugged Perfection. "Now This," He Murmured, Closing His Eyes As The Mud Cooled His Skin, "Is What I Call A Proper Soak. Far Better Than Any Royal Bath In The Kingdom."

Who Needs A Fishing Pole When You've Got Organic Ogre Gas?" He Wiped A Tear Of Mirth From His Cheek, Chuckling At The Glorious Absurdity.
